title: 12-hour and 24-hour clock
examples: When do we use a.m. and p.m.?
How do I change 7:45 p.m. to 24-hour time?

explain.say: Today we learn about two ways to tell time. One is the 12-hour clock. The other is the 24-hour clock.
We use a.m. for times from midnight until noon. This is the morning time period. For example, waking up at 7:00 a.m. is in the morning.
We use p.m. for times from noon until midnight. This covers the afternoon and evening. For instance, eating dinner at 6:00 p.m. is in the evening.
To change from 12-hour to 24-hour time, we add twelve to the p.m. time. Remember to change 12:00 p.m. to 12:00 and 12:00 p.m. to 00:00.

faq.a: A.M. stands for ante meridiem, which means before midday. It covers the time from midnight up to noon.
P.M. stands for post meridiem, meaning after midday. It covers the time from noon up to midnight.

faq.q: How do I change 3:00 p.m. to 24-hour time?
faq.a: You add twelve to the hour number. So, three plus twelve equals fifteen. The time is 15:00.

faq.q: What time is noon in 24-hour time?
faq.a: Noon is exactly 12:00 p.m. In 24-hour time, we write this as 12:00.

faq.q: What time is midnight in 24-hour time?
faq.a: Midnight is 12:00 a.m. In 24-hour time, we write this as 00:00.

facts: The 12-hour clock uses a.m. for morning and p.m. for afternoon.
The 24-hour clock uses numbers from zero to twenty-three.
Noon is 12:00 p.m. and is 12:00 in 24-hour time.
Midnight is 12:00 a.m. and is 00:00 in 24-hour time.

quiz.why: A.M. times are the same in both clocks, so it stays eight thirty.

wrong.0: This is a common mistake because students sometimes add twelve to all times.
wrong.1: This confuses the time period, mixing a.m. with p.m. notation.
wrong.2: This incorrectly treats the time as if it were midnight.

quiz.why: For p.m. times, you add twelve to the hour, so four plus twelve is sixteen.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds twelve and then adds one more, going over the twenty-four mark.
wrong.2: This mistake happens when students subtract twelve instead of adding it.
wrong.3: This forgets to change the time period from p.m. to the 24-hour format.

quiz.say: If a train leaves at 11:59 p.m., what is the time in 24-hour format?
quiz.why: You add twelve to eleven, which is twenty-three. The minutes stay the same.

wrong.1: This mixes the 24-hour number with the 12-hour designation.
wrong.2: This forgets to convert the time from p.m. to the full 24-hour system.
wrong.3: This incorrectly calculates the time as if it were one minute before midnight.
